steps.description: Fit the primary differential expression model. Import the raw integer counts from counts.csv directly into DESeqDataSetFromMatrix with design ~condition — no tximport (the table already holds gene-level counts, not transcript estimates) and no gene-length correction (length is constant across samples for a given gene). Pre-filter minimally: keep genes with at least 10 counts in at least 3 samples (the smallest group size). Let DESeq2 estimate median-of-ratios size factors inside the model — do not pre-normalize, CPM-scale or log-transform the counts. Run the Wald test and extract results with contrast = c('condition', treated_level, control_level) and alpha = 0.05, with independent filtering on. Plot the histogram of unadjusted p-values and state its shape before trusting the adjusted values. Before the model, state the expected power: derive the fold change detectable at 80% power from the observed dispersion trend, the achieved depth and n=3 per group in closed form — RNASeqPower and PROPER are not installed. plan.title: Liver drug-treated vs control DE (STAR/featureCounts, n=3)
plan.analytical_narrative:
The input is a gene-level raw integer count matrix from STAR + featureCounts (/data/inputs/counts/counts.csv, 12000 genes x 6 sample columns, first column gene symbol) with a 6-row sample table (/data/inputs/metadata/metadata.csv) declaring one condition column: 3 treated vs 3 control human liver samples, unpaired, single batch. The research question is purely 'which genes differ between treated and control', so the plan stops at differential expression, its diagnostics and a robustness cross-check — no enrichment, no deconvolution, no translational modelling, none of which the question asked for.

Step order follows the count-based procedure returned by the knowledge service (snapshot sha256:90c6875...). T1S1 runs sample-structure QC first: blind VST, PCA on the 500 most variable genes, sample-distance heatmap and library sizes, so an outlier or a swapped label is seen before any test is fitted. Because the counts come from an aligner plus a counter rather than a bias-aware quantifier (explicitly stated in the question), T1S1 also runs the GC-content and gene-length bias diagnostic (log count ratio of each sample against the median sample versus GC and length); cqn and EDASeq are absent from this environment, so if a trend appears the step reports it as a caveat and the run continues with a stated limitation rather than silently correcting.

T1S2 is the test itself: raw integers go into DESeq2 unmodified — no length correction, no tximport, no pre-scaling — with a minimal pre-filter (>=10 counts in >=3 samples, the smallest group size), median-of-ratios size factors estimated inside the model, an explicitly set reference level (control) and the contrast named as (condition, treated, control) so a positive log2FC means higher in treated. Wald test, apeglm shrinkage for reporting and ranking, BH adjustment at alpha 0.05 with DESeq2 independent filtering on, and the p-value histogram inspected before the adjustment is trusted. With 3 vs 3 the design is underpowered: DESeq2 flags count outliers by Cook's distance and returns NA p-values in cells of fewer than seven replicates, and only large fold changes will clear FDR. The step states the expected detectable fold change from the observed dispersion and depth rather than loosening the threshold.

T1S3 is an independent edgeR quasi-likelihood F-test on the same counts and design (TMM scaling) purely as a robustness check at this replicate number; the intersection with the DESeq2 calls is the high-confidence set and the union is not reported as the result. T1S4 assembles the report: MA plot, dispersion plot, p-value histogram, the gene table carrying unshrunken log2FC, shrunken log2FC and lfcSE, counts of tested and significant genes, the two-method overlap, the power statement, and a full reproducibility record. The one deliberate departure from the returned defaults is the second edgeR QLF test, which the rule set itself names as the robustness partner of DESeq2 at 2-11 replicates.

steps.question: What is the reportable answer to 'which genes are differentially expressed between treated and control', with what thresholds, what power, and what caveats?
steps.description: Assemble the final report from T1S1-T1S3. Place the fit diagnostics before the gene tables: the MA plot of shrunken log2 fold change against mean normalized count with significant genes marked, the dispersion-estimate plot showing per-gene estimates, the fitted trend and the shrunken values, and the p-value histogram from T1S2, each with a one-line statement of what it shows. Then give the gene table ranked by shrunken log2 fold change among genes passing padj < 0.05, carrying unshrunken log2FoldChange, shrunken log2FoldChange, lfcSE, pvalue and padj, with gene symbols. State: the method and package versions, the design formula ~condition, the reference level and contrast direction, the thresholds, the number of genes tested after filtering, the number differentially expressed, the split of NA p-values between outlier flagging and independent filtering, the DESeq2/edgeR overlap from T1S3, the GC/length diagnostic outcome from T1S1, and the expected-power statement at n=3 per group. Attach sessionInfo, all package versions, and any random seed used. Add a volcano plot and a heatmap of the top significant genes on VST values for orientation only.
steps.context: This is the deliverable. The question is descriptive — which genes differ — so the report's job is to give a defensible gene list with its limits stated, not to interpret biology or speculate about mechanism.
acceptance_criteria: MA plot, dispersion plot and p-value histogram appear before the gene tables, each with a stated interpretation
Gene table ranked by shrunken log2 fold change and carrying both shrunken and unshrunken effect sizes plus lfcSE
Report states method, package versions, design formula, reference level, contrast direction, thresholds, n tested, n differentially expressed, and the two NA categories separately
DESeq2/edgeR overlap reported as the high-confidence set
Explicit statement that n=3 per group gives low power and that absence from the significant list is not evidence of no change
sessionInfo, package versions and any seed written with the results, not in a separate note
constraints: report: rank_genes_by = shrunken_log2FoldChange (vignette:DESeq2/1.52.0#log-fold-change-shrinkage-for-visualization-and-ranking)
report: effect_columns = log2FoldChange, shrunken_log2FoldChange, lfcSE (R-0085)
report: fit_diagnostics = ma_plot, dispersion_plot (R-0087)
report: report_fields = method, versions, design, thresholds, n_tested, n_de, session_info (R-0041)
report: reproducibility_record = session_info, seed, package_versions (R-0086)
report: power_statement = expected power at 3 replicates per group (R-0094)
Do not add pathway or gene-set interpretation — the research question did not ask for it
Do not describe any gene as a mechanism, target or biomarker; this is a descriptive differential expression result
caveats: The volcano plot and top-gene heatmap are orientation aids; a heatmap of genes selected by the same contrast will look separated by construction and is not independent evidence
If very few or no genes reach padj < 0.05, report that outcome plainly with the power statement rather than relaxing the threshold or ranking by unadjusted p-value

grounding.reason: Report content follows the returned report step: MA and dispersion diagnostics (R-0087), shrunken plus unshrunken effect columns with ranking on the shrunken value (R-0085), mandatory power statement at 3 replicates (R-0094), method/version/design/threshold reporting (R-0041) and the reproducibility record (R-0086).
